mandatoryRequirements.rvpReproPolicy: 1) When RVP_repro is Yes: the issue reproduces on the Intel Reference Validation Platform (RVP), meaning there is a high likelihood the defect appears across most OEM customer units designed on that RVP platform (critical platform-wide impact) -- explicitly highlight 'also reproduced on RVP' in the CMF reasoning and recommendation justification. 2) When RVP_repro is No, NA, Not available, or Pending: normalize display to 'RVP repro: No'; do NOT penalize or reduce the 6-category mathematical score (a high-scoring customer-unit blocker >= 3.50 with B>=3 and D>=3 still qualifies for CMF_OK), and state in the reasoning that RVP repro is currently No (isolated to customer unit / not yet reproduced on RVP).

dimensions.name: Severity
dimensions.rubric: 4=Catastrophic / System Crash: Cannot power on or boot; BSOD / kernel crash; system hard hang or freeze; unexpected reboot/shutdown; permanent black screen / no display; data loss/corruption; permanent HW damage; certification/WHQL failure OR Major Subsystem / Core Feature Loss: Core subsystem unusable (audio, camera, Wi-Fi/BT, USB-C/TBT port dead); persistent display flickering or blanking until app/session closes; failed sleep/wake (S0ix/S3/S4); severe performance/thermal throttling. 3=Moderate / Intermittent Functional Degradation: Momentary or intermittent display flicker/glitch; single application hang/crash; specific feature or wake-word misses intermittently while OS stays responsive; moderate performance degradation. 2=Minor Functional / Warning: Minor UI artifact, brief single-frame visual blip, wrong LED behavior, or Device Manager/event-log warning with limited functional impact. 1=Cosmetic / Negligible: Cosmetic issue, typo, wrong status/description string, or internal debug log note with negligible functional impact.

dimensions.name: Occurrence
dimensions.rubric: 4=Always / Consistent (90%-100%): Reproduces on every attempt (always_100%) or >=90% of test cycles across units; at least hourly SW failure OR Frequent (50%-89%): Reproduces in 50%-89% of cycles (frequently_50%-90%, e.g., 6/9 cycles) across multiple UUTs or configurations. 3=Occasional / Sporadic (10%-49%): Reproduces in 10%-49% of cycles (sporadic_10%-40%, e.g., 2/7 cycles); recurring intermittent failure. 2=Rare / Very Sporadic (<10%): Reproduces in <10% of cycles (very_sporadic_<10%, e.g., 1/20 to 1/100 tries; <1 failure per 40 hours SW). 1=Isolated / Seen Once (<1%): Seen only once (once), <1/5000 cycles, or cannot be reliably reproduced.

dimensions.name: Detection
dimensions.rubric: 4=Universal / Desktop & Idle Flow: Triggered on boot to desktop, idle state, or opening any standard app/file; immediately and easily visible to every end user OR Daily Core Workflow: Triggered during common daily user actions such as login/logout, S0ix sleep/resume, AC adapter plug/unplug, dock attach/detach, or voice wake.S4/S5 hibernate, restart 3=Specific Feature / Secondary Workflow: Triggered during a specific feature flow, OOBE, AFT, multi-monitor mode switch, or heavy GPU/CPU stress workload. 2=Corner-Case / Single App Button / Stress: Triggered only when clicking a specific button in one non-core app, unusual multi-step sequence, or synthetic corner-case stress. 1=Lab / Debug Setup Only: Requires special debug steps/settings/device, non-preloaded test tool, or unique manufacturing process.

dimensions.name: Recovery
dimensions.rubric: 4=No Runtime Recovery: No acceptable workaround or runtime recovery exists; failure persists across reboots or permanently blocks the device OR Hard Reset / Disruptive Recovery: Requires forced power-button hold (4s/10s shutdown), AC/battery pull, BIOS reflash, or OS reinstall; or symptom remains continuously while any app/file is open.Recovery requires warm system reboot, 3=App Restart / Replug:  closing/restarting the affected app, or unplugging/replugging the device. (SW/driver updates are fixes, not runtime recovery.) 2=Simple User Action / Undocumented: Simple, reliable user action resolves the issue immediately with minor inconvenience, or runtime recovery is not documented. 1=Automatic / Transparent Recovery: Fully effective automatic self-recovery with negligible usability or validation impact.

dimensions.name: Business Impact
dimensions.rubric: 4=Launch / Phase Exit Gate: Production halt, launch blocker, or showstopper blocking FVT/SIT phase exit; executive OEM escalation; financial/brand risk; multi-platform impact OR Validation Blocked / Milestone Risk: Customer milestone at risk; blocks a key customer validation test suite (HLK, feature FVT, stress sign-off); multiple escalations likely. 3=Moderate Program / Support Risk: Delays a non-gating test case; single-project scope with a viable debug path; customer dissatisfaction, support burden, or warranty exposure possible. 2=Low Business Exposure: Isolated corner-case observation in a single app or lab setup; does not block customer milestone sign-off or phase exit. 1=No Business / Customer Impact: Internal-only observation with no identified customer validation or schedule impact.

dimensions.name: Customer Experience
dimensions.rubric: 4=System or Core Experience Unusable: Laptop or core feature (display, audio, touch, keyboard, Wi-Fi, boot) is unusable in normal daily use (e.g., persistent display flickering whenever desktop/apps are open) OR Severe Visible Disruption: Significant visible degradation that materially disrupts normal tasks (e.g., repeated full-screen flicker on AC plug/unplug, frequent audio drop, or forced reboot losing unsaved work). 3=Noticeable User Annoyance: Intermittent visible degradation; user notices the flicker/glitch or must restart an app/peripheral, but the system remains usable. 2=Minimal User Impact: Minor visible annoyance or isolated to a rare single-app button that normal users rarely encounter. 1=Not Visible to End User: Debug-only symptom, internal status mismatch, or invisible to end users.

dispositionTable.meaning: Clear customer must-fix issue with substantial combined technical, customer, and business impact.
dispositionTable.requiredAction: Approve as CMF; assign owner, target, containment, and customer communication.

dispositionTable.meaning: Borderline issue requiring cross-functional judgment because one or more dimensions are moderate or incomplete.
dispositionTable.requiredAction: Review evidence, scope, requirement, and customer commitment; document rationale.

dispositionTable.meaning: Low combined exposure, narrow trigger, simple recovery, or limited customer/business effect.
dispositionTable.requiredAction: Track through the standard defect process; reassess if scope or impact increases.

dispositionTable.meaning: One or more core categories cannot be scored from the available ticket evidence.
dispositionTable.requiredAction: Request missing reproduction, recovery, or impact details from the submitter before disposition.

dispositionTable.minimumConditions: Duplicate sighting or merge ID identified in ticket/comments
dispositionTable.meaning: Issue reports the same underlying failure already tracked under a primary sighting.
dispositionTable.requiredAction: Mark as cmf_duplicate and link to the primary sighting.

gatingGuardrails.name: Low business or narrow trigger cap
gatingGuardrails.rule: If B <= 2 OR D <= 2, the issue cannot be CMF_OK and is capped at CMF_REVIEW.
gatingGuardrails.rationale: Prevents a severe symptom in a rare, lab-only, or low-business scenario from being automatically approved.

gatingGuardrails.name: Mandatory escalation
gatingGuardrails.rule: Safety, security/privacy, data loss/corruption, permanent hardware damage, or certification/WHQL launch blocker is at least CMF_REVIEW regardless of score.
gatingGuardrails.rationale: Prevents a weighted average from hiding unacceptable consequences.

gatingGuardrails.name: Incomplete evidence
gatingGuardrails.rule: If any category cannot be scored from evidence, return INCOMPLETE rather than assigning a low score.
gatingGuardrails.rationale: Unknown information is not evidence of low risk.

gatingGuardrails.name: High normal-flow UX exception
gatingGuardrails.rule: A persistent normal-flow issue with B = 4, CX = 4, and D = 4 may qualify as CMF_OK when the weighted score is >= 3.50 even if Severity is 3.
gatingGuardrails.rationale: Allows major user-facing failures to be recognized without requiring a crash-level technical severity.

gatingGuardrails.name: Occurrence discipline
gatingGuardrails.rule: Use actual fail/attempt cycles and unit/configuration counts. Do not increase Occurrence solely because the symptom is severe.
